note: Single source of truth for timing, text, stats, camera and sound. docs/utah-rain/beat-sheet.md is generated from this file. Captions use **bold** for the key number and \n for the line break. Every real-world number is sourced in docs/utah-rain/sources.md (codes U1…).
intro: The rain, runoff and flooding are imagined; Utah's geography, rivers, basins and drainage are real. The day chip (“Day 1 … Day 30 · imagined scenario”) is an illustrative timeline, never a forecast, and every animated consequence on a map is labelled “imagined scenario”. Beats without a sourced number show a qualitative gauge instead (runoff, ground saturation, flood pressure), as the brief asks. Source codes (U1…) point to `docs/utah-rain/sources.md`.
resets: Canyon close-up (1) · globe (2) · tilted map of the south (3) · cliff diorama (4) · cut-away block (5) · inside a slot canyon (6) · top-down statewide divide map (7) · fly-to Lake Powell (8) · Great Salt Lake (9) · mirror-flat salt flats, low and white (10) · a city on transparent ground (11) · crane up over the Wasatch (12) · colour shift: the sun breaks through (13) · jump in time: months later (14).

beats.title:
What if it rained in
Utah for 30 days?
beats.caption:
The desert turns green.
Then the valleys start filling
beats.visual: Close on red sandstone as the first heavy drops hit and darken the rock. Within 2 s the dry wash below fills: a thin turquoise sheet becomes a rushing channel between the canyon walls.

camera.shot: Low wide shot, slow push-in down the wash
camera.reason: Starts on the brief's image (rain on sandstone) and lets the change happen in frame by 3 s

beats.caption:
Utah normally gets about
**13 inches** a year

stat.label:
of rain and snow, statewide
yearly average · NOAA

beats.visual: Pull out to the globe: the American West, Utah outlined. Storm clouds spin up over the state, then the globe gives way to the flat terrain map (fly-to, no cut).

camera.shot: Orbit on the globe, then fly down to the state
camera.reason: Where in the world, then into the map without teleporting

beats.caption:
A dry landscape suddenly has
water everywhere
beats.visual: Tilted terrain map of southern Utah: dusty red relief, dry washes lighting up as thin turquoise threads, temporary pools mirroring the clouds, and patches of green spreading where soil allows.

camera.reason: Shows that it is happening across the whole region

beats.caption:
Waterfalls pour into canyons up to
about **2,600 ft** deep

stat.label:
deep at most, Zion Canyon
(half a mile) · NPS

beats.visual: Miniature Zion cliff: ribbon waterfalls pour off the sandstone rim, tiny plants push out of cracks, a still pool at the bottom reflects towering storm clouds.

camera.shot: Crane up the cliff face, waterfall to rim
camera.reason: "It keeps going": the scale of the walls

beats.caption:
The narrowest places collect
the biggest rush
beats.visual: Cut-away terrain block: rain falls across a broad plateau, runs into tributaries (animated turquoise flows), and converges into one slot canyon.

camera.reason: A 3d cross-section shows how wide rain becomes one narrow flow

beats.caption:
Narrows walls rise **1,000 ft**
over a 20–30 ft river

stat.label:
canyon walls; the river is
sometimes 20–30 ft wide · NPS

beats.visual: Inside the slot canyon: a turquoise surge fills the floor of an empty canyon; two tiny hikers watch safely from a high bench on the rim.

camera.reason: Builds tension, then reveals the hikers safe above

beats.caption:
Some water leaves.
Some has nowhere to go

stat.label:
of Great Basin that drains
inland, never to the sea · NPS

beats.visual: Visual reset: top-down terrain map. The real drainage divide draws on; the southeast tints toward the Colorado River system, the west toward the Great Basin. One set of arrows flows off the map; the other stops in lakes and valley floors.

camera.reason: Only a map shows the two systems side by side

beats.caption:
Downstream waits Lake Powell, about
**186 miles** long when full

stat.label:
long at full pool,
Lake Powell · NPS

beats.visual: Fly-to the southeast: arrows ride the Colorado and its tributaries into Lake Powell, whose winding arms brighten as the water rises (imagined) and continue downstream past the state line.

camera.reason: Follows the water that has somewhere to go

beats.caption:
The old shoreline becomes
a memory

stat.label:
usual size; about 2,300 at
the 1986 record high · USGS

beats.visual: Tilted map of the lake: rivers swell (the Bear, Weber and Jordan), the shoreline creeps across the lowest ground first, flooding mudflats and leaving higher ground dry. An outline marks the old shore.

camera.reason: Shows the lake growing unevenly, following the terrain

beats.caption:
About **30,000 acres** of salt flats
turn into a mirror
beats.visual: Visual reset: low angle across white salt crust under a thin sheet of water, mirroring the storm sky; the Silver Island Mountains on the horizon.

camera.shot: Low wide shot, slow lateral track
camera.reason: The mirror only works close to the surface

beats.caption:
The streets follow our plans.
The water follows gravity

stat.label:
of Utahns live along the
Wasatch Front (about)

beats.visual: Miniature Salt Lake City on a transparent ground: under the street grid, the buried creeks, slopes and low points glow turquoise as mountain runoff arrives; storm drains brim and low roads take water.

camera.reason: The 3d orbit shows the hidden land under the grid

beats.caption:
Wetlands spread where about
**10 million** birds stop yearly

stat.label:
migratory birds a year at Great
Salt Lake and its wetlands

beats.visual: Crane up from the city to the Wasatch Range and out over the lake's edge: temporary wetlands and green patches spread across the valley floors; flocks wheel over shallow water.

camera.reason: "It keeps going": from the streets to the whole landscape

beats.caption:
On day **30**,
the clouds finally break
beats.visual: The clouds part and warm low sun crosses the state (the one lighting change). Pull back over Utah: red-rock waterfalls, greener desert patches, a larger Great Salt Lake and flooded valley floors shining.

camera.shot: Pull back to a tilted statewide view, low hero sun
camera.reason: The big reveal of the whole transformed state

beats.caption:
The rain stopped.
The transformation didn't

stat.label:
acre-ft a year leave the lake
only by evaporation · USGS

beats.visual: The calendar runs on: green fades back to red, pools shrink, inland water slowly evaporates and soaks in, and pale sediment rings stay behind, echoing the ancient Lake Bonneville shorelines on the mountains.

camera.shot: Slow drift, holding the wide view
camera.reason: Lets the slow change be the point

beats.visual: The landscape dims softly behind a large neutral question.

camera.reason: Gives the question room to land

beats.endCard:
Explore the greener Utah,
or wait for the
water to recede?
